item.title: RC’s Vander Veen repeats as TVL MVP
item.description: Ripon Christian senior Jake Vander Veen has repeated as Trans Valley League boys basketball MVP.

item.title: Buffs complete sweep of Sierra
item.description: Manteca got six runners on base in the first three innings Friday at Sierra but only had one run to show for it. That all changed in a six-run fourth inning due in part to Devon Richardson’s three-run home run, and the Buffaloes never looked back in a 12-3 win in Valley Oak League baseball action at Jack Thomson Stadium.

item.description: There is no doubt in Manteca Councilman Mike Morowit’s mind that drivers on Lathrop Road routinely run red lights at the Union Road intersection.

item.title: YOSEMITE AVENUE: THE KEY TO IT ALL
item.description: Yosemite Avenue is the problem — and represents the greatest potential — for any plan to set the stage for transforming downtown Manteca.

item.title: Manteca Fire Dept. aims to restore its ISO fire rating to Class 2
item.description: The Manteca Fire Department is pursuing a goal in the coming months of restoring a “2” rating the city once had from the Insurance Services Office.

item.title: Water deal could help fish, farmers, pay for SSJID work
item.description: Efforts over the years to modernize irrigation water delivery and reduce water waste has put the South San Joaquin Irrigation District in a position to assist south of the Delta farmers as well as allow for more robust fish flows on the Stanislaus River.

item.title: Lancers’ historic NorCal run ends in semifinal
item.description: The deepest run of any East Union basketball team in school history ended Saturday night, as the Lancers fell to the Menlo-Atherton Bears 68-38 at the Dalben Center in Division III Northern California Regional semifinal action.

item.title: Spartans pull away late to reach NorCal Division IV final
item.description: No. 3 Lathrop scored the first 10 points of it their NorCal Division IV semifinal tilt, only for No. 10 Benicia to battle back and take an eight-point second-quarter lead. The Spartans righted the ship for a halftime tie thanks to a pair of consecutive 3-pointers by Faith Butler, and after six lead changes and three ties in the second half, the Spartans pulled away for a 55-48 win and a ticket to Yuba City to face No. 1 Faith Christian in the NorCal final on Tuesday night at 7.
